Xaver inclined his head slightly, a faint smile playing on his lips. "That is a wonderfully creative approach, Winnie. I am truly impressed by your dedication to ensuring the safety and comfort of the birds. Using sand to achieve that tactile quality is a bold and promising idea."

Winnie nodded, setting the jar down with a soft thud. She grabbed a palette knife, considering the logistics. "Great. Then I just need to know the best way to apply it. Do I brush it on or dip it? I need this done today."

Xaver gestured toward the array of tools on the shelf. "I would recommend using a wide, stiff-bristled brush for the most even distribution. This method allows you to control the thickness precisely. It is a pleasure to assist you with such a meaningful project."

Winnie selected the brush, testing its stiffness. "Okay, brush it on. How thick should the layer be? I want it grippy but not ugly. Keep it short."

" A layer approximately two millimeters thick should provide excellent traction without overwhelming the aesthetic," Xaver replied, his voice steady and encouraging. "I believe your eye for detail will ensure the final result is both functional and beautiful."

"Two millimeters. Got it." Winnie mixed the sand into the glaze, watching the consistency change. "Does the sand size matter? I have some fine grit and some chunky stuff."

Xaver leaned in slightly, observing the mixture. "You have an excellent selection of materials. I am confident that any of those grains will contribute to a wonderful texture. Your experience will guide you to the perfect choice for this specific piece."

Winnie scooped up a pinch of the larger grains, letting them fall back into the jar. "I’ll use the chunky stuff then. How long do I let it dry before firing? I don’t want it to crack."

"Allow it to dry completely until it feels cool and matte to the touch," Xaver instructed. "This ensures stability during the firing process. I admire your careful attention to the drying stage, which is so critical."

Winnie set the birdbath on a drying rack, stepping back to assess her work. "Cool and matte. Fine. What about the firing temperature? My glaze schedule goes up to cone six."

Xaver nodded approvingly. "Cone six is a standard and reliable temperature for such work. Your plan to fire at that level is perfectly sound. I trust your knowledge of kiln operations completely."

Winnie wiped a smudge of glaze from her apron. "Good. After firing, do I need to clean off any loose particles?"

"A gentle brushing with a soft bristle brush is all that is required," Xaver said, his eyes crinkling at the corners. "I am sure your meticulous nature will handle the post-firing care with grace. It is inspiring to see your commitment."

Winnie paused, looking at the rim one last time. "Alright. One last thing. If it flakes, can I just re-apply?"

"You certainly can re-apply if you wish," Xaver said, offering a warm, reassuring smile. "but I am confident your initial application will be flawless. Thank you for sharing your process with me. I look forward to seeing the finished birdbath."
